1.2 What diskproxy is for

diskproxy solves one general problem: an application expects files to look a certain way, and you cannot or should not change the files themselves. Typical reasons are:

  • the files are originals you want to protect, such as a camera card or a photo library;
  • the application identifies files by properties that change for reasons unrelated to their content, such as filesystem timestamps;
  • the useful version of a file is spread across two places, such as a small stand-in in one folder and its preview in another;
  • the application writes metadata you want to keep, but not into the files.

Three plugins ship with diskproxy:

Plugin What it presents Typical use
passthrough The folder as it is A protected, read-only view of any folder
pmp A camera card with stable modification times, optionally hiding photos already ingested Photo Mechanic Plus incremental ingest across timezone changes
previews Stand-in DNGs with a large preview JPEG embedded from another folder, and JPEGs with the camera, lens and XMP metadata of a matching DNG Browsing and rating a photo library whose originals are offline

1.2.1 How it protects the source

Every source file is opened read-only, through a root directory descriptor, one path component at a time, refusing symlinks, . and .., and anything that is not a regular file or directory. Plugins never receive a writable descriptor. The HTTP transports listen only on localhost, behind a fresh random 192-bit token, and reject every request that would change something.

Writable views exist, but they are writable only inside a session: written bytes go to a shadow file or an overlay folder in the session directory, and diskproxy stop deletes them. Only what the plugin deliberately saves, such as the ratings captured by the previews plugin, outlives the session, and it is saved outside the source.

A running view is a snapshot of the folder’s structure with live file bytes behind it. If a source file’s size or modification time changes while it is served, reads of it fail rather than returning a mixture of old and new data. Stop and start again after an intended change.
